checks.name: Publication rule and audit sourcing
evidence: The rule logic is correct. A verified audit plus a detector apply or suggest of the same sign, or an abstention, publishes. An opposite suggest or apply (including a guard-refused apply) or a conflict holds. With no audit, only a guarded apply publishes.

Sourcing: audited_signs is an argument to run_sign_application. _audits() checks only that the sign is int +-1 and that audit_task is done in the backlog. It does not check that the task established that sign for that dataset and channel.

Demonstrated on the synthetic group: audited_signs={'hip_power': {'sign': -1, 'audit_task': 'GT24-C02'}} (an unrelated done task). hip_power abstains, so it published with multiplier -1 (basis 'audit').
Audited signs are also outside bound_build(). The same bound code with different adapter-supplied signs publishes differently, so a pilot does not bind the signs.

Fix: a committed audited-signs table (dataset, channel, sign, audit_task, citation, per-recording exceptions) read once and included in bound_build(), with a link test that each audit task's backlog record cites its entry. Adapters pass only the dataset key, not signs.

round_1.summary: The core is sound. Only guarded apply signs change data, and they change it by exact negation. Outputs never alias inputs, and dtype, shape, NaN and signed-zero round-trip bit for bit through undo. Parameter overrides are refused, and the detector is executed from exactly the bytes that were hashed. Four things send it back: (1) the full-mode pilot gate accepts a hand-built dict with any 64-hex receipt string, any 'verified_by' text and the current bindings, so it can be forged; (2) a numpy masked array loses its mask, and masked values come out as data; (3) the guard re-counts families with the detector's own FAMILY_GROUPINGS and PLATE_TIMING_TESTS, so a family-table bug passes both; (4) the design note is stale on the launcher and claims evidence arrays are hash-checked when they are not. D-CORE-11-1 is not ready to copy. It fails the schema (no task_id or status). Its option C does not say what happens when the detector suggests or conflicts against the audit. Under José's standing preference for standardized names by default, 'leave out' options A and B are not neutral, so the question may not need asking. No research data were read.

checks.name: Can any path change data beyond an apply sign?
evidence: Synthetic fixture from tests/test_sign_application (apply on knee_angle -1, ankle_angle +1, hip_moment +1, ankle_moment +1, ankle_power -1).
No output shares memory with its input. The same array object under two channel names gives independent outputs.
float32 and float16 inputs keep their dtype. A Fortran-ordered input gives identical values (C-contiguous output; the hash is order-normalized).
NaN and +0.0 round-trip bit for bit through undo. An unknown channel name abstains and is returned unchanged. Integer arrays are refused.

Fail: a numpy.ma.MaskedArray input (10 masked samples whose underlying data were 9999.0) comes out as a plain ndarray. The mask is gone and 9999.0 appears as data, because np.asarray strips the mask. That changes data beyond a sign. The hook should refuse ndarray subclasses (require type(a) is np.ndarray), or carry masks explicitly.

Note: the verdicts differed between float64 and float32/float16 copies of the same synthetic data. The detector converts to float64 internally, so rounding moved some borderline votes. This is not a hook defect, but adapters should pass channels at their stored precision and not downcast.

checks.name: Guard independence
checks.evidence: guard_apply independently re-checks the combine step: two or more agreeing families, no moderate/strong or documentation dissent, claimed families covered by supporting evidence, min_families >= 2. A combine bug that applies on one family is caught. But the family assignment uses det.FAMILY_GROUPINGS and det.PLATE_TIMING_TESTS from the detector module. Demonstrated: remapping hip_stance_extension to 'joint_anatomy' in the detector table makes the guard accept 'joint_anatomy + marker_geometry'. Per-test sign errors (a test voting the wrong sign) are outside any guard that reads the detector's own evidence; they are covered only by the pilots. Fix: give the hook its own frozen family table, covered by the hook hash, and a test that it equals the detector's; a divergence then fails loudly.

checks.name: Build binding and TOCTOU
checks.result: pass for the detector; minor gaps for the policy, table and hook
evidence: load_bound_detector reads the file once, hashes those bytes and executes the same bytes, so the declared hash describes the code that ran.

The policy module is executed from one read (_load_policy), but bound_build() re-reads every file (file_sha256), and split_documentation re-reads refuted_documentation.json itself. A change between reads makes the logged hashes not describe what ran.
HOOK_PATH is hashed from disk, not from the imported module's source.
The backlog (task status) controls withholding but is outside the build. The design note discloses this, and the log records each statement's action.
Fix: hash the policy bytes that were executed, read the refuted table once (pass its bytes or verify its hash after use), and record the hook's hash at import.

checks.name: Undo exactness and log tampering
checks.result: exact; tampering is undetectable without an external anchor
checks.evidence: Undo checks output_sha256, negates or copies, and checks input_sha256, which is exact (NaN, -0.0, dtype). A consistently tampered log (multiplier flipped, input_sha256 recomputed) passes undo and 'restores' the wrong array. Integrity therefore rests on the log's sha256 being recorded elsewhere (write_json_exclusive returns it for the manifest). Recommend an expected_log_sha256 argument to undo, checked against the manifest value.

checks.name: Pilot gate
checks.evidence: check_pilot_record accepts any dict with dataset, outcome 'passed', a non-empty verified_by, any 64-hex launcher_receipt_sha256 and bindings equal to the current bound_build(). A hand-built record with verified_by 'nobody' and receipt '0'*64 let mode='full' run and apply 4 signs. The existing test uses 'a'*64. Required: load the pilot record from a committed audit file; check that the guarded-launcher receipt file exists, hashes to launcher_receipt_sha256 and lists the same bindings; and tie verification to backlog status done for the pilot task (the same authority the documentation policy uses), not to free text.

checks.name: Decision D-CORE-11-1
evidence: Schema: validate_backlog rejects it as written ('decision.task_id: expected nonempty text'); with task_id 'CORE-11' and status 'queued' it validates.
Order ('channels published under the rule, fewest first') is neutral and stated. Labels and consequences do not name the recommendation, and decide_before_recommendation is true.

Completeness: C is underspecified. It stops only when an applied sign contradicts the audit; it does not say what happens when the detector suggests the opposite sign or conflicts on a channel where the audit has a sign. A safe C holds such a channel for review instead of publishing it.

Is a decision needed? José's standing preference: signals go under standardized names by default when evidence supports the sign, and 'leave out' is not a neutral option. His 2026-10-30 instruction makes verified audits authoritative over README statements. Every pilot dataset has verified per-channel audits (UM21-C03, GT21-C01, GT23-C02, GT24-C02), so C with a review hold on detector disagreement is that preference applied. The coordinator can adopt it as a logged policy application. If a question is still wanted, it should ask only about the disagreement handling, and A/B should say what evidence would unblock the held channels.
Minor: the 'check' text is fine, but the consequence counts (343 of 648) cite only the GT21 pilot.

checks.name: GT21 sheet fixes at 1100 px and in a 390 px iframe
checks.evidence: The AB24 chip now reads '1 recording left out: its plate file starts 1 ms after the kinematics; dropping one sample would recover it'. Figure 3 uses grey for out-of-band headings, not red. No horizontal scroll at 390 px (content width 373 px). The other rules are unchanged from the GT21 pilot round.

required_fixes: Pilot gate: verify a committed pilot record file, the launcher receipt file (exists, hash matches, same bindings), and backlog done status for the pilot task. Add tests for a forged receipt and for a free-text verifier.
Refuse ndarray subclasses (masked arrays, matrices) or preserve masks explicitly; add a test.
Guard: the hook's own frozen family table, plus a test that it equals the detector's table.
TOCTOU: hash the executed policy bytes, read the refuted table once, and record the hook hash at import.
Design note: remove the stale 'until that review, nothing is launched' (UM21-T02 is done_for_launcher), and either hash-check evidence arrays or remove that claim.

D-CORE-11-1: add task_id and status. Define C's handling of a detector suggest or conflict against the audit (hold for review). Reconsider whether the question is needed given José's standardize-by-default preference; if asked, A and B must state what evidence would unblock the held channels.
recommendations: Document that adapters must not downcast channels before the hook.
